$schema_note: Machine-readable project state. Source of truth for design; CLAUDE.md is the human-readable view of the same content. When the two disagree, fix one to match the other — don't let drift accumulate.

project.name: reddit_research
project.purpose: Personal Reddit research tool. Single user (Eli's developer account). The use case is: search subreddits for important / useful information for an LLM to summarize.
project.status: v0.1.0 tagged + deployed on warehouse-vm 2026-05-05. v0.2 chunk 1 (MCP stdio server adapter) merged on main 2026-05-07/08, panel-cleared (round 10: Codex/Gemini/Opus all approve after fixes). 71/71 unit tests + live JSON-RPC handshake verified. Repo at https://github.com/elib100/joeblow-research; production install under redditmcp user at /home/redditmcp/reddit-research/ still on v0.1.0 (not yet pulled to v0.2). Next: v0.2 chunk 2 markdown preprocessor (Phase 0 measured ~10x token leverage), then production pull. Reddit API access form pending from 2026-04-27, no longer blocking.

decisions.choice: Python 3.11+
decisions.rationale: Matches existing portfolio on the deploy host.

decisions.choice: httpx against Reddit's public .json endpoints (no OAuth, no PRAW)
decisions.rationale: Sidesteps Responsible Builder Policy approval gate (Nov 2025+). Returns same JSON shape as OAuth API. Exposes X-Ratelimit-* headers cleanly (which PRAW hides). Structurally read-only. Verified 2026-04-27 across all needed endpoints (listings, search, threads+comments, /api/morechildren). See docs/json_endpoint_findings.md.

decisions.choice: OAuth + PRAW deferred to future upgrade only — not in MVP
decisions.rationale: Useful only for higher rate limits or write capability — neither is an MVP requirement. Reddit API access form submitted 2026-04-27; if approved, OAuth becomes a SLOT-IN ADDITION to the .json transport, not a replacement.

decisions.choice: SQLite single file, WAL, busy_timeout=5000, PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL
decisions.rationale: Same operational pattern as collector/warehouse on the deploy host. Handles CLI-vs-MCP contention.

decisions.choice: none for MVP (.json endpoints are unauthenticated)
decisions.rationale: No client_id/secret/password to manage. Configuration has no secrets. Future OAuth flow is documented in .env.example as commented-out keys for the upgrade path.

decisions.choice: PEP 621 pyproject.toml, src/ layout, pip install -e . for dev
decisions.rationale: Modern standard. Required for CLI entry point and future MCP server import.

decisions.choice: stdio only, accessed remotely via SSH
decisions.rationale: Eliminates network listener attack surface. Remote access via 'ssh warehouse reddit-mcp'.

decisions.choice: core library → CLI → MCP server
decisions.rationale: CLI provides cheap debug + personal-use surface. MCP is thin glue on top once core is proven.

decisions.choice: cache by default (opt-out), fresh=True per-call to bypass
decisions.rationale: LLM shouldn't have to think about caching ergonomics. Fast-by-default is the point.

decisions.choice: three flat TTLs, no age-aware computation
decisions.rationale: Variable age-aware TTL was overengineered for the 'don't need data for long' research workflow. Add age-awareness later if it proves valuable.

decisions.choice: raw parsed JSON dicts as Reddit returned them
decisions.rationale: .json transport returns plain HTTP responses; no client-library translation layer means what's cached is what's served. Earlier PRAW-based plan needed the 'normalized objects' framing — that's moot now.

decisions.choice: cache key includes all retrieval params + normalization_version suffix
decisions.rationale: Without this, get_thread(top=20) cache-poisons get_thread(top=100). Discovered in second panel review.

decisions.choice: 403/404 cached 24h, 5xx never cached
decisions.rationale: Permanent vs transient. Caching 5xx would poison after one Reddit blip.

decisions.choice: validate ^t[1-6]_[a-z0-9]+$ in core, not at MCP boundary
decisions.rationale: CLI gets the same protection as MCP. Cheap.

decisions.choice: read X-Ratelimit-* on every response; back off proactively at <10% remaining; honor 429 Retry-After
decisions.rationale: .json transport exposes the headers cleanly, which removes the PRAW-hides-them problem. Manual backoff is straightforward when headroom is visible.

decisions.choice: single dedicated call to /r/<sub>/comments/<thread>/_/<comment>.json (depth/limit params)
decisions.rationale: Cleaner than tracking 'more' markers + /api/morechildren — one HTTP call returns the comment with its full reply subtree in context. Matches MCP-friendly 'follow this comment' semantics.

decisions.choice: official `mcp` Python SDK (FastMCP) over hand-rolled JSON-RPC
decisions.rationale: MCP protocol surface (initialize / tools/list / tools/call / shutdown / capabilities) is a moving target with discovery semantics and JSON-schema conventions. FastMCP owns it; we own the Reddit logic. Optional dependency (installed via `[mcp]` extra) so plain CLI installs stay light.

decisions.choice: Reddit-domain errors return as structured `{ok: false, error: {type, ...}}` dicts; only programmer / infrastructure failures raise (and become MCP `isError: true`)
decisions.rationale: Raising surfaces as `isError: true` on the CallToolResult, which loses the discriminator fields (reason, retry_after, kind/used/cap, status) that the LLM needs to decide what to do next. Round-10 panel agreed unanimously this is the right split.

decisions.choice: one WorkflowBudget per stdio process; LLM-callable `reset_budget` tool zeros consumption (caps unchanged)
decisions.rationale: CLAUDE.md ## Rate-limit-discipline says 'per-session for the MCP server'. The host process exit is the session boundary; `reset_budget` is the LLM's escape hatch for new logical research runs within one session. Round-10 Codex flagged this as a self-bypassable guardrail; declined for single-user pragma — the alternative (server restart) is operationally costly.

decisions.choice: lazy-import `mcp` SDK in `mcp/__main__.py`; print friendly install hint and exit 1 if missing. `mcp/__init__.py` does NOT eagerly re-export from `server.py`.
decisions.rationale: Round-10 Codex P1: an unconditional eager import from `__init__.py` crashed plain installs (without the `[mcp]` extra) on `import reddit_research.mcp`. Lazy-import gives the user `pip install 'reddit-research[mcp]'` instead of a stack trace.

decisions.choice: encode numeric bounds in MCP tool argument schemas via `Annotated[int, Field(ge=..., le=...)]`; keep core-side runtime validation as the backstop
decisions.rationale: Hosts that respect schemas fail-fast on out-of-range args (depth>5, limit>100 etc.). Core validation still protects direct Python callers (CLI, library). Round-10 Codex+Gemini agreed.

operations.name: search
operations.signature: search(query, subreddit=None, sort='relevance', time='all', limit=25, fresh=False)
operations.returns: list[ThreadSummary] (title, score, author, sub, num_comments, permalink, fullname, created_utc)

operations.name: get_thread
operations.returns: Thread (post + top N top-level comments by score, no sub-tree expansion)
operations.notes: Cheap by design. LLM picks promising top-level comments to follow up on.

operations.name: expand_comment
operations.returns: CommentTree (one comment + N levels of replies)
operations.notes: The 'follow promising sub-trees' operation. Aggregate per-workflow budget also applies. Subreddit is needed for the URL; resolved from a previous get_thread call's response.

operations.name: status
operations.notes: last_seen_headroom is the {used, remaining, reset_in_seconds} dict from the most recent X-Ratelimit-* response, or null if no calls have been made yet. last_call_status is the most recent HTTP status code (200, 429, 5xx, etc.) or 'none' if no calls have been made.

columns.name: cache_key
columns.notes: includes all retrieval params + normalization_version (e.g. ':v1' suffix)

columns.name: body_json
columns.notes: raw parsed JSON as Reddit returned it (the .json endpoint response), or error metadata {reason, message, error} for non-200

ttl_table.notes: Only 403/404 are cached as errors. 5xx and network errors are never cached.

per_workflow_aggregate_budget.scope: per-process for CLI; per-session for MCP

security.secrets_at_rest: none in MVP — .json transport is unauthenticated. Cache dir mode 0700, owned by deploy user only.
security.mcp_network_exposure: none — stdio only, remote access via SSH
security.input_validation: fullname pattern ^t[1-6]_[a-z0-9]+$ (or bare [a-z0-9]+) enforced in core before reaching HTTP layer
security.write_safety: structurally impossible through .json transport — no write endpoints exposed. Write-flag plumbing returns only if/when OAuth is added later.
security.cross_context_isolation: personal vs Motroco data: hard isolation by deployment. Separate service users, separate cache.db per use context. Enforced by Unix file permissions. See historian's personal/CLAUDE.md.
security.transport_lockout_risk: Reddit could block unauthenticated .json access at any time without warning. Mitigation: design core/client.py so transport is swappable; OAuth (when granted) is the slot-in replacement.

mcp_server.status: v0.2 chunk 1 merged on main 2026-05-08, panel-cleared (round 10), not yet deployed to production
mcp_server.transport: stdio only — no network listener; remote access via `ssh warehouse reddit-mcp`
mcp_server.error_envelope: Reddit-domain errors return as `{ok: false, error: {type, ...}}` with discriminator fields (reason / retry_after_seconds / path / kind+used+cap / status). Error types: budget_exceeded, rate_limited, not_found, forbidden, redirect, transport_error, upstream_error, http_error (catch-all for unmapped statuses), invalid_id, invalid_input, no_budget_configured. Programmer/infra errors raise → MCP `isError: true`.
mcp_server.schema_bounds: depth (0-5), expand_comment.limit (1-50), search/listing/thread limit (1-100), purge.older_than_days (>= 0) — encoded in pydantic Field annotations on tool params; core enforces same bounds at runtime as backstop for direct callers.
mcp_server.session_lifecycle: one Operations + one WorkflowBudget per stdio process lifetime. reset_budget tool zeros consumption (caps unchanged) for new logical research runs without restarting the host process.

deferred_to_v0_2_or_later: preprocessed views (markdown transforms for token savings) — v0.2 chunk 2
OAuth + PRAW transport (only adds value if Reddit grants access — for higher rate limits or write capability)
async (httpx async client — straightforward to add)

panel_reviews.scope: v0.2 chunk 1: MCP stdio server adapter (commit 419810e)
blockers: Codex P1: optional-dep / unconditional surface mismatch — `mcp` SDK in `[mcp]` extra but `reddit-mcp` script + `mcp/__init__.py` re-export installed unconditionally; plain installs crashed on `import reddit_research.mcp`.
Gemini P1: Cache.purge(older_than_seconds=-1) made cutoff > now, so `WHERE fetched_at < cutoff` matched every row — silent total cache wipe. CLI argparse was the only guard.
panel_reviews.blockers_resolution: commit 2cef169. (1) Drop eager re-export in mcp/__init__.py; mcp/__main__.py lazy-imports server module and prints `pip install 'reddit-research[mcp]'` install hint with exit 1 when SDK missing. Verified in clean venv. (2) Cache.purge raises ValueError on negative input; MCP `purge` tool encodes ge=0 in pydantic schema for fail-fast, catches the runtime ValueError as `invalid_input` envelope.
blockers_declined: Gemini P1.2: WorkflowBudget thread-safety (TOCTOU on api_calls += 1). Verified at mcp/server/fastmcp/utilities/func_metadata.py:95 — sync tools dispatch directly in the async event loop, no to_thread. Stdio is single-stream serial; no race. Adding a Lock would be premature for hypothetical future requirements.
should_fix_applied: Add HTTPError catch-all in _wrap_reddit_call: unmapped statuses (400/401/418/etc.) become structured `http_error` envelopes with status preserved instead of escaping as MCP isError (Opus P2).
Encode numeric bounds in MCP tool schemas via `Annotated[int, Field(ge=..., le=...)]` (Codex+Gemini P2).
Enforce upper bounds (1-100) on search/listing/get_thread limits in core (Gemini P2). Reddit silently truncates above 100 anyway; closes prose-vs-code contract gap.
Extract shared `_to_jsonable` to `reddit_research._serialize.to_jsonable` so CLI and MCP can't drift on serialization shape (Gemini P2).

Six new tests for previously-uncovered error-envelope branches: rate_limited (with retry_after_seconds rename), redirect (location), upstream_error (5xx), transport_error (httpx exception), parser-strict ValueError (Reddit schema drift), unknown-status http_error envelope. Plus cache.purge negative guard. (Opus+Codex P2)
should_fix_declined: Codex P2: gate `reset_budget` behind a startup flag or remove from tool surface. Declined per single-user pragma — the budget is a per-research-run guardrail by design, restarting the server for legitimate multi-run sessions is operationally costly.
Gemini P2-3: split parser-strict ValueError vs cap-violation ValueError into distinct envelope types. Declined — message disambiguates; adding a SchemaError class is more churn than payoff.

session_log.outcome: Pushed initial commit to github.com/elib100/joeblow-research (MIT license, README, full design docs, spike script). Submitted Reddit API access request via support form with personal-research framing. Awaiting Reddit response — target 7 days.

Tested Reddit's append-.json public endpoints with curl + identifying UA. All needed shapes work (subreddit listing, search-in-sub, search-all, thread + comments, /api/morechildren). Same JSON shape as PRAW. X-Ratelimit-* headers exposed cleanly (~100 calls per 10-min sliding window). 404/403 distinguishable, 403 includes structured `reason` field. Cookieless and stateless. Findings in docs/json_endpoint_findings.md.

Changed primary transport from OAuth+PRAW to httpx + Reddit .json endpoints. Reasons: (1) eliminates Responsible Builder Policy approval bottleneck, (2) solves panel's previous PRAW-hides-headroom concern, (3) smaller dependency footprint, (4) structurally read-only (no write-flag plumbing needed in MVP), (5) better error data via `reason` field. Trade-offs: write capability and user-context operations require OAuth (deferred to upgrade path); Reddit could block unauthenticated .json at any time (mitigated by swappable transport design). Rewrote CLAUDE.md, README.md, .env.example, requirements-phase0.txt, phase0_spike.py. Operations API stays the same shape; cache layer / caps / key normalization unchanged. Spike is now runnable immediately with no Reddit account setup.

Spike against live Reddit confirmed: bogus thread IDs return 403 (not 404, surprise — locked into core/errors.py mapping); r/lounge returns 403 with reason='gold_only'; pagination after-cursor works (zero overlap between pages); /api/morechildren.json works with capped child list; expand endpoint with context=0 returns focal subtree only; no redirects observed across test cases (so follow_redirects=False in v0.1 is safe). Signal-to-noise ratios measured: list_only ~24%, list_plus_threads ~10%, expand_one ~16% — confirms ~10x token leverage opportunity for v0.2 markdown preprocessor. Findings persisted to docs/json_endpoint_findings.md.

Wrote cli/__main__ + cli/commands (argparse adapter for the six operations + two output formats + typed-exception → exit-code mapping). Wrote tests/run_qa.py (37 unit tests with mocked HTTP + tmpdir SQLite) and tests/smoke_test.py (live one-shot).

Found 1 P1 (get_thread comment-budget undercount on nested replies) + 4 P2 (CLI _run not catching ValueError/RuntimeError, --depth help mismatch, missing positive-int validation, missing happy-path expand_comment test). All applied. Suite expanded to 48 tests.

Codex blocked on 2 P1: bad 200s cached before parsing (could poison cache for full TTL on Reddit schema drift), and budget charged before _proactive_backoff (could charge with zero upstream call). Both applied: _call_and_cache replaced with _fetch_with_cache (parses first, caches only on success); spend_api_call moved into the retry loop after backoff (charges per actual httpx attempt). Opus + Gemini approved without changes. Suite expanded to 51 tests.
